name: Climatarian diet

lead: A climatarian diet picks foods for low greenhouse-gas emissions. In practice that means limiting ruminant meat such as beef and lamb, favouring chicken, pork, fish and plants, and choosing local produce.

Its appearance angle is indirect: diets lower in processed food and saturated fat, and higher in vegetables, are associated with healthier weight and complexion. Research on the diet itself concerns environmental impact and how easily people adopt it.

paras: Followers reduce or drop beef and lamb, keep moderate amounts of lower-impact meats and fish, and emphasise locally grown fruit and vegetables. It is often described as a flexible form of meat reduction rather than a strict rulebook.

Because the rule centres on emissions rather than nutrients, nutrition depends on food choices, and people replacing red meat should plan for iron, B12 and protein. Evidence on flexitarian-style patterns is largely observational.

angle.text: The diet is chosen for its carbon footprint, but its practical shape of less red and processed meat and more produce overlaps with patterns associated with healthier weight. Any appearance effect depends on the overall diet.

lead: The climatarian diet is a dietary pattern designed to minimise environmental impact, chiefly by reducing high-emission foods such as beef and lamb [1][2]. People who follow it for their looks usually do so as a flexible, produce-heavy way of eating that can support weight management and skin health, though the diet's own stated goal is environmental.

A 2023 review comparing six popular US diets found the vegan, climatarian and Mediterranean diets had the lowest environmental impacts, attributed to less ruminant meat and processed food, and that moderate chicken, pork and fish alongside locally grown produce could be maintained without raising carbon footprint [1].

A 2021 study that prescribed omnivores one of four meat-reduction diets, including a climatarian diet limiting beef and lamb, found all groups reduced meat intake in the following weeks [2]. A 2026 study in Turkey developed a 25-item scale to measure adherence to the diet [3].
infobox: Limit beef and lamb; choose low-carbon foods

paras: Climatarian eating treats a food's emissions as the main selection criterion. Reviews describe it as relying less on ruminant meat and processed food and more on locally grown fruit and vegetables [1]. It is related to flexitarian eating, in which plant foods dominate and limited meat is allowed.

The 2023 review reported that diets with lower carbon footprints also tended to have positive health effects, with the lowest footprints for vegan, climatarian and Mediterranean diets [1]. It compared findings from literature and representative meal plans rather than testing people on the diet [1].

In a prescribed-diet study, the vegetarian group ate significantly less meat than the three flexitarian groups during a seven-day adherence period, yet all groups lowered meat intake afterwards without significant differences between them [2]. Attitudes toward meat and animals also shifted [2].
No studies found testing the climatarian diet for appearance outcomes. Related research is limited to environmental modelling [1], meat-reduction behaviour [2] and an adherence scale [3].
